Which text makes conciliation before the conciliation office (مكتب المصالحة) a prerequisite to any individual labour claim (Law 90-04, around art. 19), and is the requirement framed as a condition of admissibility of the claim?

What counts as an individual labour dispute under Law 90-04 (its first articles: a dispute between one worker and the employer on the performance of the employment relationship), as opposed to a collective dispute governed by Law 90-02?

Which workers and employers fall outside Law 90-04: civil servants and agents of public administrative bodies (governed by their own statute and the administrative judge), and whether some categories have their own conciliation procedure.

Is there a prior internal step inside the employer's organisation (internal procedures for handling grievances, referral to the hierarchical superior with a short reply period) before the referral to the labour inspector?
How is the conciliation office seised: referral by the worker to the labour inspector (written request or oral statement recorded), and within what period the inspector convenes the office.
When the office meets, the time limits for the conciliation meeting, and the summons of the parties (and second summons after a first absence).
What happens when the defendant (employer) fails to appear after summons: is a record of non-conciliation drawn up for absence?
What happens when the plaintiff fails to appear: is the request struck out or recorded?

Exceptions to the conciliation requirement: the defendant residing outside the national territory; the employer in judicial liquidation (or bankruptcy / settlement); possibly other exceptions in the CPCA.

What the record (محضر) must contain: record of conciliation (total or partial) and record of non-conciliation, and that a copy is delivered to the parties; the record of non-conciliation is the document to attach to the petition.

Effect of a conciliation agreement: executory force, the period for its execution (around 30 days), and the request to the president of the social section to order execution with a penalty payment if it is not executed.

Time limit to bring the claim before the social section after the record of non-conciliation: six months from the delivery of the record (CPCA, around art. 504), and the sanction: forfeiture of the right to bring the claim.
Whether that six-month period is a forfeiture (سقوط) or a limitation; whether it can be suspended or interrupted; whether the court raises it of its own motion or only on a plea.
How the six-month period is counted: from the day of delivery of the record, month to month, and what happens when the last day is a holiday (CPCA rules on counting procedural periods).
Missing or unknown date of delivery of the record: what the lawyer must check (the date written on the record or the receipt).
Competent section: the social section (القسم الاجتماعي) of the court has exclusive jurisdiction over individual labour disputes (CPCA, around art. 500).

Territorial jurisdiction: the court of the place where the work is performed, or the worker's domicile when the contract is suspended or terminated because of a work accident or occupational disease (CPCA, around art. 501); whether this rule is of public order.
Composition of the social section: a judge with assessors representing workers and employers, and the consequence of its composition for the validity of the judgment.
First hearing to be held within a short period after filing (around 15 days) and the duty to decide quickly; not a filing condition but useful context.

Matters decided in first and last resort by the social section (annulment of disciplinary sanctions decided without the statutory procedure, delivery of a work certificate or pay slips) and matters subject to appeal.
Provisional execution of right of certain labour judgments (wages and allowances for the last months), and the use of urgent relief before the president of the social section.
Dismissal claims: Law 90-11 art. 73-4 (reinstatement or compensation for a dismissal in breach of the procedure or without cause); the conciliation step still applies before such a claim.

Disputes that look like labour disputes and are not: social security disputes (their own prior recourse before the committees, Law 08-08), collective disputes (Law 90-02), civil servants' disputes before the administrative court, commercial disputes between a company and its manager who is not an employee.
Claims by the employer against the worker: does conciliation also apply when the employer is the plaintiff?
Required documents: the record of non-conciliation (or proof of an exception), the employment contract or proof of the employment relationship, pay slips, the dismissal decision.
Whether a petition filed without a record of non-conciliation is inadmissible (عدم قبول) and whether the defect can be cured during the proceedings.
Whether the court must raise of its own motion the absence of the prior conciliation step (public order) or only on the defendant's plea.

Amendments: Law 90-04 amended by Law 91-28; CPCA (Law 08-09) replaced the old Code of Civil Procedure on 25 April 2009 and contains the social section rules; possible later amendments to Law 90-04 (2022) introducing new conciliation rules.
Limitation of wage claims themselves (civil code periodic payments) as distinct from the six-month forfeiture after non-conciliation: belongs to the periods module.
